observation_summary: The StringUtils.equals method fails when comparing different CharSequence implementations (e.g., String vs StringBuilder) because it relies on the default Object.equals() behavior, which is not guaranteed to be content-based for all CharSequence types.
hypothesis: The StringUtils.equals method uses the default Object.equals() implementation for CharSequence objects, which is insufficient because CharSequence implementations (like StringBuilder) do not necessarily override equals() to perform content-based comparison. The fix requires implementing a character-by-character comparison.
prediction: The production code will show a direct call to cs1.equals(cs2) or similar, failing to handle non-String CharSequence types correctly.
experiment_rationale: The bug report explicitly states that StringUtils.equals relies on undefined behavior by calling CharSequence.equals(Object). The failure in the test case (comparing String to StringBuilder) confirms that the current implementation does not perform a content-based comparison.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a procedural error in the implementation of the equals method. It uses an incorrect algorithmic approach (relying on object identity/default equals) instead of the required content-based comparison for the CharSequence interface.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While it involves a check, the core issue is the lack of a proper comparison algorithm for the CharSequence interface, not just a missing guard.
